name: Scarlett 2i2 ("2x2")
notes: Focusrite has never sold a 'Scarlett 2x2'; retailers describe the 2i2 as a 2x2 (2-in/2-out) interface. No 2i2 generation has MIDI ports (the 2i4 does). Testing is audio-domain: inputs, outputs, preamps, phantom power, monitoring.

drivers.name: Built-in USB Audio 2.0 class driver usually works for 2nd–4th gen (no ASIO); 1st gen needs the Focusrite driver

serviceManual.notes: Focusrite does not publish service manuals or schematics. Community repair info only (GroupDIY, iFixit; 1st-gen op-amp supply regulator MIC5205 U4 is a known fix).

failureModes: Scratchy gain pots / skipping gain encoder (4th gen)
Phantom power failure or switching thump
USB dropouts, crackle, worn USB socket

tests.name: Device enumeration
steps: Connect via the supplied USB cable directly to a computer port (no unpowered hub).
Confirm the USB/power LED is lit.
Windows Sound settings: the Scarlett appears as playback AND recording device.
Open Focusrite Control / Control 2 and note generation, firmware and driver version in the notes field.

tests.name: Confirm no MIDI port (expected)
steps: Press Enable MIDI in MIDItest.
The Scarlett should NOT appear as a MIDI input/output. If it does, note the port name – it may be a 2i4.

tests.name: Line outputs L/R and channel identity
steps: Connect monitors or headphones. Turn MONITOR and headphone knobs to about 9 o'clock.
Choose the Scarlett as audio output, then play Left, Right and Both.
Confirm each tone only comes out of the correct side with no crackle.

tests.name: Headphone output balance & pot
steps: Play 'Both' tone from the output test.
Sweep the headphone knob slowly min→max: level must change smoothly, no crackle or dropouts.
Check left and right are equally loud; wiggle the plug gently for intermittent contact.

tests.name: Monitor level pot sweep
steps: With the tone playing, sweep MONITOR fully min→max.
Listen for scratchiness, one-sided drop-out or sudden jumps.

tests.name: Input 1 / Input 2 signal and noise floor
steps: Choose the Scarlett as audio input and start the meter.
With nothing plugged in and gain at minimum, record the noise floor.
Feed a source into Input 1 only, then Input 2 only. Each meter must respond only on its own channel.
Halo LED should go green with signal, amber/red when driven hot.

tests.name: Gain pot / encoder sweep
steps: Feed a steady signal into each input.
Sweep gain min→max slowly while watching the meter: level must rise smoothly with no dropouts or crackle.
4th gen: confirm the encoder does not skip steps and Auto Gain sets a sensible level.

tests.name: INST / LINE mode
steps: Plug a guitar or line source via 1/4" jack into each input.
Toggle INST: level/tone should change and the INST LED follow the switch on both channels.

tests.name: Phantom power (48V)
steps: With a condenser mic (or phantom tester) on XLR, switch 48V on: red 48V LED lights and the mic works.
Optional: measure ~48 V on XLR pin 2 and pin 3 to pin 1.
Switch off/on and listen for excessive thumps or ongoing noise.

tests.name: AIR mode (3rd/4th gen only)
steps: Toggle AIR on each channel: the LED lights and the input gets brighter (4th gen: Presence and Drive modes).
Mark Skip on 1st/2nd gen.

tests.name: Direct monitor
steps: Plug headphones in, speak/play into Input 1.
Direct Monitor ON: you hear the input with no latency. OFF: it disappears (unless a DAW monitors it).

tests.name: USB stability (10 minutes)
steps: Keep the output tone and input meter running for 10 minutes.
Gently flex the USB cable at the socket. Any dropout, click or device disconnect = fail (worn socket or cracked joints).

tests.name: Front panel LEDs & buttons
steps: Check every halo, 48V, INST, AIR, Direct and USB LED lights.
Press each button several times: it must toggle reliably every press.
